[nation]Stuipendia[/nation]

[spoiler=Agnieszka]

The soft chord from the wind chimes that resonated throughout the courtyard was not one of lightheartedness, but rather one of quiet contemplation.

Keeper Agnieszka sat on a bench in the courtyard of one of the Church's libraries, reading through the browned pages of one of the codexes she borrowed; as she read, she took notes on a small notepad. Accompanying her were other Keepers, each searching for the answer to their own questions within old tomes of great wisdom and newer books.

She wrote down one more line of notes and stood, walking to return the codex to the library. As she moved, her white religious robes flowed like silk in the wind, and the thin rows of golden scripture in the black sash that wrapped around her waist shimmered like ten thousand tiny stars.

[/spoiler]

The plane touched down in Stuipendia, and out from it stepped Keeper Agnieszka. She was here to fulfill an agreement to share knowledge which had been signed by the diplomats of the two nations in the years prior. In her left hand she carried a leather tome of knowledge and a notebook, and secured on her black sash was a pen. She walked into the governmental building of the city she arrived in.

[quote=new_westmore;61398152]"I don't know, probably about 20 minutes at the most- Oi! Take a turn into the inlet here, it links up to the lake!"[/quote]
The ship turns, and loose objects wobble in its great turning. Al-Upran has little to say, perhaps sea sickness, perhaps exhaustion with these foreigners. They could not say, and he did not speak. Twenty minutes passed, the man rose and cracked his neck. He stepped up and out first, he looked towards the great moon above.

The plane touched down in Stuipendia, and out from it stepped Keeper Agnieszka. She was here to fulfill an agreement to share knowledge which had been signed by the diplomats of the two nations in the years prior. In her left hand she carried a leather tome of knowledge and a notebook, and secured on her black sash was a pen. She walked into the governmental building of the city she arrived in.[/quote]
The great hum is the first thing she notices; it sounds like a computer, no, a hundred thousand servers performing a great hymn. A call to something beyond this world, to the Mechanical Hyperuranion. A manufactured divinity, the waiting and the man-made. Before us, and formed from our hubris. She feels watched, the cameras leer at her, yes, and the locals are aware of her dress but are unquestioning of Li and his calling to a foreign Imperium. But this was something else entirely. She was not talked to, excluding the airport attendants, even then they seemed stiff. But here, this tower, the Freed Workers Tower, it screams. It sings hymns, not to her God, perhaps not to any God, but its existence worshipped something. It had to. A veritable Tower of Babel.

As she walked in the door, it got louder; the secretary greeted her. Stiff, like an automaton. 

[i]"Ah, you must be the Keeper, yes? [u][b]He[/b][/u] will see you now, just step into the elevator!"[/i]

The elevator was emblazoned with the sigil of Technocratic Socialism.
